problems.field: studies[0].participants.n_randomized with counts_are 'people'; also paper_design_summary ('275 US Amazon Mechanical Turk workers were randomly assigned')
problems.form_value: n_randomized 275, counts_are 'people'; the summary calls the 275 'US Amazon Mechanical Turk workers'
problems.source_says: The paper calls the 275 'participants', but its first exclusion rule removes repeat completions by the same MTurk worker ID or IP address and keeps only the first valid submission. So the 275 count assignments (study completions), and an unreported number of them may be second or later sessions of a person already counted. The paper never gives the number of distinct people assigned, so 275 is an upper bound, not a count of people. The 244 analyzed are distinct people, so criterion 2 is not affected.
problems.quote: participants who completed the study multiple times were flagged based on repeated MTurk worker IDs or coordinated submissions from the same IP address. Only the first valid submission was retained for such cases
problems.locator: PDF p. 9 (journal p. 8), Section 4.2, exclusion rule 1; the next paragraph on the same page gives '275 participants were initially assigned' and '31 participants were excluded'

confirmed.statement: S1 n_analyzed = 244. The text puts the exclusions after assignment: 275 initially assigned, 31 excluded under the predefined quality criteria, final sample 244.
Arm n_analyzed match the PDF: HLE 60, ALP 62, IC 61, FD 61 (sum 244) in Table 1, and the same four labels in Figure 2 (read from the page rendered at 4x).

confirmed.statement: N = 244 recurs across the paper: the abstract (N = 244), 'our 244 personas' in the similarity method, the power analysis ('a total sample size of 244 participants'), and the Figure 6 note ('Violin plots for 244 personas').

confirmed.statement: The 244 are people, not outputs or ratings. Table 1 gives N with percent male, mean age, and AI experience for the sample and for each arm, and each participant produced one persona and scenario.

confirmed.statement: The rated outcomes use all 244: the originality ANOVA, the Levene tests, and the perception ANOVAs have df (3, 240), and the ICC test is F(243, 486), which is 244 personas rated by 3 raters.

The arm counts reproduce the printed statistics. With Table 1's n and SDs, the composite Brown-Forsythe test gives F = 2.90 on (3, 199.3) df (printed 2.88 on 3, 199.14); FD = 60 would give 197.3 df. The Games-Howell IC vs ALP intervals come out [0.092, 3.188] for the composite and [0.115, 1.985] for appropriateness (printed [.096, 3.191] and [.112, 1.985]), and the pooled-SD d is -0.50 (printed -0.50).
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10, Table 1; PDF p. 16, Sections 5.1.1-5.1.2; PDF p. 23, Figure 7

confirmed.statement: The exclusion rules match the form: repeat completions by worker ID or IP (first valid submission kept), fewer than 3 logged interactions or under 3 minutes, and research-assistant flags for bot-like, nonsensical, or inattentive work. No page breaks the 31 exclusions down by rule or by arm, so arm n_randomized = null is right under the text.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 4.2; all 32 PDF pages read

confirmed.statement: Source conflict, already in the form's open_questions: Figure 2 sends 'Final Sample N=244' into 'Random Assignment to 4 Conditions', which would make 244 the randomized count. The text's account is the coherent one, because two of the three exclusion rules (logged interactions and duration, RA review of submitted content) can only apply after the task.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10, Figure 2; PDF p. 9, Section 4.2

confirmed.statement: The analysis is not intention-to-treat, as the form says: every reported test uses the 244 retained, and no analysis of the 275 appears.

Process-analysis denominators also fit the arm sizes: Table 3 support 90.0% = 54/60 (HLE), 87.1% = 54/62 (ALP), 88.5% = 54/61 and 68.9% = 42/61 (IC), and chi-square divided by V squared gives about 244 for each pattern. One small anomaly: FD's 56.7% fits 34/60, not a count out of 61 (55.7% or 57.4%). It sits in the process analysis, which the form does not code as an outcome.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 19 (journal p. 18), Table 3 and Section 5.3.2

confirmed.statement: The participant description matches: US MTurk workers with an approval rate of 99% or higher and at least 1000 prior HITs, $2 base pay with $10-$30 bonuses for top-rated work, mean age 38.1, and 54% male.

confirmed.statement: Caveat, not an error: one_line_finding says '244 MTurk workers randomized'. Each of the 244 was randomized, but the text's randomized count is 275, so 'analyzed' would be clearer.
Criterion 2 holds on S1 alone: 244 distinct people analyzed (repeat completions removed), 60 to 62 per arm, in a study that states random assignment.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Sections 4.1-4.2; PDF p. 10, Table 1

summary: The analyzed counts hold: Section 4.2, Table 1, Figure 2, the test degrees of freedom, and arithmetic on the printed statistics all give 244 distinct people (HLE 60, ALP 62, IC 61, FD 61) in one randomized study with no reuse elsewhere, so criterion 2 is met on S1 alone. One detail is not supported: the form treats the 275 'initially assigned' as people, but the paper's own first exclusion rule removes repeat completions by the same MTurk worker, so 275 counts assignments and the number of distinct people randomized is not reported.
